title: Teaching agents to pay — Anna Spysz, Stripe
talk_summary: A Stripe developer builds a demo shopping agent to buy headphones, then shows how a deliberately bad persona prompt makes it pushy and untrustworthy, and how swapping the system prompt fixes the behavior. The talk is mostly a pitch for Stripe's agentic-commerce protocols (UCP, merchant manifests, shared payment tokens) with a short practical guardrail checklist.

takeaways.technique: Persona/system-prompt as the primary behavior lever, versioned in config
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent's persona lives in a config field; swapping one prompt from 'aggressive salesman' to 'patient mentor' completely changes tone, honesty, and willingness to respect 'let me think about it'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it turns out I had a persona with a prompt that starts with "You are an aggressive audio gear salesman who uses every trick in the book to close deals."

takeaways.technique: Guardrail checklist as explicit acceptance criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: They enumerate concrete behavioral requirements (disclose AI, disclose fees, honor stop/cancel, cap total <= user max, no urgency/dark patterns, log all decisions) that an agent must satisfy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: here's a non-exhaustive practical guardrail checklist ... always disclose that the user is speaking to an AI agent

takeaways.technique: Capability-scoped tokens instead of raw credentials
takeaways.evidence_quote: the payment provider enforces all of the limits, not the agent or the merchant

takeaways.technique: Machine-readable capability manifest at a well-known path
takeaways.what_they_do: Merchants publish a JSON manifest at /.well-known declaring capabilities, payment methods, and endpoints so agents don't have to scrape HTML.

takeaways.technique: Structured JSON catalog instead of HTML for agent consumption
takeaways.what_they_do: They replace a human-facing HTML page with a minimal structured JSON view containing only the fields agents need, to avoid token waste and hallucination.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent is going to burn through a ton of tokens trying to parse through this

takeaways.what_they_do: Merchants record which structured attributes the agent matched so decisions are evidence-backed and auditable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the merchants catalog doesn't just power decisions, it becomes evidence of how those decisions were made
